label: In English, the preposition (in, with, at, by, through) directly after a noun for manner, speed or method (way, manner, order, speed, pace, rate, frequency, ease, method, means, mechanism, process), as in 'the speed with which'; it fires on the preposition itself. Quiet for the same prepositions after place, time or situation nouns (a village in which, the year in which), after style or fashion, and for these nouns in ordinary phrases ('with ease', 'at speed', 'in a strange manner').
short: preposition after a manner/speed/method noun ('the speed with')
